label: GO choosing a1 right after a reward that followed a non-reward (start of a reward streak)
explanation: Fires only at GO (never at D1 or D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (in_rew=1 at D1), and almost only when the agent picks a1 (model_act==1 holds 99.6% of the activation mass; a2 choices essentially never fire). GO + prev_reward==1 + a1 alone reaches recall 0.99 but precision 0.27. The strongest refinement is that the reward has to be new: when the trial two back was unrewarded, precision rises to 0.78 (dev F1 0.71, mass recall 0.73). When the trial two back was also rewarded, the feature is mostly silent (precision 0.06), so it fires at the start of a reward streak and fades as the streak goes on (e.g. 1.00, then about 0.3, then 0, over consecutive rewarded a1 trials). Most of the missed recall is at rel -3, where the trial two back is outside the window (about 21% of the mass), plus weak activations on the second rewarded trial in a row. The top activations (about 1.0) are switches to a1 after a rewarded rare transition from a2 to S1, or repeats of a1 after a reward, both while S1 is good, so the feature looks like freshly rewarded evidence for S1 that drives an a1 choice. It also fades late in the episode (trials 80+). The predicate uses only observed history plus the agent own upcoming choice, so no future variables. Magnitude: this was not checked beyond the streak decay seen in the example windows.
